item.title: SCP-071: Test-log addendum 071-2?
item.content:encoded:
On ██/██/██ Dr. █████████ selected four D-class personnel who have all self-identified as asexual since early adulthood. One of these subjects (a female survivor of [DATA EXPUNGED]) was asked to describe SCP-071's current form, and complied: "It's some kind of clearish, colorless oval blob….no obvious features or body parts…it smells like unwashed sheets, and it keeps shrinking in on itself, making this squelching noise….turn me on? Oh jeez, no…quite the opposite, Doctor, this thing scares the [REDACTED] out of me. Could I please get one of those pills ans go back to quarters?"

The remaining D-class asexuals described a similar amorphous, translucent, and foul-smelling entity; as with D- █████████, all reported that SCP-071 shrabk away from them, as if in pain.

item.title: SCP-071: SCP-071 vs. sex-repulsed asexuals
item.content:encoded: Weird idea: what if sex-repulsed aces forced SCP-071 into its actual base form and made it extremely uncomfortable? If 071 "feeds" on lust, it would logically be "poisoned" by anti-sexual thoughts and feelings; if the nearest viewer had no ideal mate or fetish to copy, 071 would be too confused to keep any shape but its natural one.

item.title: SCP-5978:
item.content:encoded:
Author, did you happen to follow the feedback-seeking process noted in the How to Write an SCP Guide? There are a lot of immediately noticeable errors, most of which could have been quickly fixed if noted before a mainsite post. For example:

SCP-5978 is a hourglass, standing 9.5 inches tall and has a 6-inch base.

  • Since "hourglass" starts with a vowel sound ("our-glass"), the article used should be "an" and not "a".
  • The Foundation is a scientific organization, and uses metric measurements. Inches are not metric measurements.
  • The parallel structure of "standing […] tall" and "has […] base" is inconsistent.
  • It's not certain what measurement for the base is. Presuming it's got a circular base, the measurement would be specified to the diameter rather than the length of a side.

The rest of the article is similarly in need of edits to maintain the clinical tone that a professional researcher would use. If you haven't looked at the feedback process yet, I highly recommend doing so if you want to submit a successful page to the mainsite.

item.title: SCP-597: Re: I'm willing to rewrite this SCP.
item.content:encoded: Creepiness, even squick, is OK up to a point in these articles: most anomalies that need to be secured and contained would freak the average person out. Still, if the Foundation can't avoid using human caretakers for SCP-597…then people with some ideal profile (physical and/or psychological) should be able to avoid the skip's psychosexual compulsions. If not, I'd recommend a fully automated containment chamber (with robots handling the care and cleaning) plus a drastic reduction of the consequences for seeing SCP-597 indirectly. (Somebody should be able to react like a disinterested adult when security footage shows a malfunctioning cleaner-bot caught in the wrong place.)
